uncited: The family shares the goal of enhancing volume visualization through stylized lighting and feature abstraction.
All methods operate on fragment-level data, typically utilizing the volume sample gradient as a proxy for surface normal orientation.

They decouple illumination from the physical light transport equation, instead using mathematical functions of the view direction, light direction, and scalar field properties to modulate color [S3857].
Common inputs include the normalized gradient $\nabla f_n$, light vectors $L$, and base colors derived from transfer functions.
The output is a final color $c$ that combines ambient/gaseous components with directed illumination effects [S3857].
Volumetric illustration differs from surface-based NPR in several important ways.
